insight.title: The Airman Who Dropped a Wrench
insight.subtitle: How a simple maintenance slip-up nearly detonated a nine-megaton thermonuclear warhead in Arkansas.
insight.notificationHook: One dropped wrench almost nuked Arkansas.

sections.text: Deep inside an Arkansas silo, nineteen-year-old Dave Powell was servicing a Titan II nuclear missile. He was using a heavy socket wrench. Suddenly, the eight-pound socket slipped from his hands, falling seventy feet.

The socket bounced off a platform and struck the missile's thin skin, puncturing a pressurized fuel tank. Rocket fuel began hissing into the dark silo, threatening a catastrophic, multi-megaton thermonuclear explosion.
Hours later, the leaked gas ignited. The massive explosion blew off the 740-ton silo door and threw the warhead into a nearby ditch. Miraculously, the safety systems held; it did not detonate.
We built the ultimate weapon, then dropped a wrench on it.
